fields.value: Emergent role differentiation without central assignment: workers shift roles based on colony need and local pheromone density.
Pheromone gradient + antennal contact. No vocalizations. Signal degrades in ~10 minutes, preventing false trails from persisting.
decentralized emergence, positive feedback with natural decay
Trail pheromone deposited on the substrate by walking foragers.
Local pheromone concentration on the ground at a branch point; a forager's branch choice is biased toward the stronger trail.
The environment: the trail on the ground. No individual ant holds the map; the state is outside the bodies.
A round trip nest -> food -> nest. A completed trip is visible to others only as added pheromone on the path walked.
Reinforcement: pheromone accumulated from completed trips, set against loss of the mark over time. A shorter path is completed more often per unit time and so accumulates faster.

cycles.path: forager walks path -> deposits pheromone -> pheromone biases the next forager's choice -> next forager walks path
food returned to nest -> colony sustains and recruits foragers -> foragers leave nest -> food returned to nest
pheromone decays -> unused path loses its mark -> fewer ants choose it -> less deposit on it

fields.value: Spending the digestive secretion on a trapped object that is not prey.
The number of action potentials fired as trigger hairs are touched: a running count of mechanical stimulations.

Staged by the count. Two action potentials: the trap snaps shut. After the second stimulus: the jasmonic acid signalling pathway is activated. More than three: genes for prey-degrading hydrolases are expressed, in proportion to the number of stimulations. Transcripts of the sodium channel DmHKT1 also depend on the number of stimulations.

fields.value: Song carries 1,000km+ through the deep sound channel (SOFAR). No other land-derived mammal communicates at this spatial scale.
Song evolves each year via social learning. New phrases originate in one region and spread across the ocean basin within a single season — demonstrating rapid, basin-wide cultural updating.
20,000km round trip annually between tropical breeding grounds and polar feeding grounds.
acoustic culture, basin-scale social coherence, intergenerational learning, seasonal cycle fidelity

stable pack with established hierarchy and pair bond at center

fields.value: Pups learn hunt coordination through direct participation alongside experienced pack members. Skills are transmitted socially across generations without genetic encoding.
Howling broadcasts territory boundaries, reducing direct conflict. Scent marking creates persistent spatial memory readable by non-pack members.
Vocalization (howl, bark, whimper) + body posture + scent marking. Multi-modal, context-sensitive.
relational hierarchy, earned trust, multi-year social bonds, distributed care of young
